description: Whether the trunk needs every residual block's activations or the last layer's alone. `shipped` is the production input (all 18 block increments through the frozen encoder, joint PCA to 128). `final384` is the final trunk state at the correct cell — the 384 channels the engine's own heads read — standardized and unrotated (act_source=trunk_final, pca_dim=0); `final128` is the same channels through the joint PCA at the shipped width. The single-layer arms need auxiliary/rating_dev/extract_last_block.py run first. EVERY ARM HOLDS OUT WHOLE PROBLEMS, since this is a feature-side question and a held-out problem's parameters come from the trunk alone. The arms run at FOUR SEEDS (a fifth shipped arm finished before the panel was cut short): within a seed the arms hold aside the same problems and their delta is paired, across seeds nothing may be subtracted. THE SHIPPED ARMS ARE ALSO THE BASELINE FOR A LATER ENGINE-NETWORK COMPARISON: an arm added to this manifest under the same seeds, on the same machine, before the next fetch_database, holds aside the same problems and pairs against them without the shipped arms being re-run. The panel reaches the held-out likelihood only — it re-maps no ranks and projects no per-cell vectors, so it says nothing about declared-rank agreement or the motif readings, both of which a change of activation source would also move. `tf3final512` is the ENGINE-NETWORK arm: the final trunk state of kata1-tf3-b10c512-s3203M-d5937M, its 512 channels standardized and unrotated, to be read against `final384` — the same layout on the shipped network — and not against `shipped`. The two differ in width as well as in network, so the contrast is between the networks AS THEY WOULD BE USED, not at a matched input dimension.
